answer.new_information: The record relays the same SemiAnalysis report already held in e101 (Kyber delayed to 2028 on PCB midplane manufacturability; NVL72x2 two-Oberon-rack alternative scrapped after cloud and hyperscaler pushback). Not previously stored: the more powerful four-die Rubin Ultra version has been cancelled, leaving only the two-die version at roughly half the real-world compute; CPO-NVSwitch will not arrive until Feynman, the generation after next, so Nvidia lacks a proven way to scale Rubin Ultra to very large systems for now; Nvidia plans to make up the shortfall with more Oberon-Rubin racks in the existing form factor (this last point is The Decoder's own sentence, not SemiAnalysis). Period and mapping: the texts do not state that the four-die cancellation is the Kyber NVL144 configuration, so it bears on Kyber only as a condition risk, not as a confirmed Kyber change. All of it is SemiAnalysis rumour with no Nvidia confirmation; Nvidia's only response is that its roadmap is intact.

arguments.statement: Lean No: Kyber NVL144 is more likely than not to be unlaunched by 2027-12-31. SemiAnalysis (rumour, relayed by CNBC, DCD and The Decoder as one report, not independent) reports the delay to 2028 because the PCB midplane remains hard to manufacture (e64, e66, e98, e100, e101, e70, e71), against a 2027 original slot (e99). Nvidia's 'roadmap is intact' statements (e65, e72, e102) contradict the delay but give no date or specifics. The new report adds that the four-die Rubin Ultra has been cancelled and CPO-NVSwitch is deferred to Feynman, which further weakens the 2027 case if they bear on Kyber; the mapping to Kyber is not stated.
limitations: SemiAnalysis rumour relayed by several outlets; one source, not independent confirmation
Nvidia denies the delay but gives no date, so the denial is non-specific
Four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation is not tied to Kyber in the texts
Period: the delay is to 2028, a stated year, not a month
what_would_change_it: Nvidia or a customer confirming a Kyber NVL144 launch or shipment date in 2027
A filing or official product announcement giving a Kyber timeline
Independent supply-chain confirmation that the PCB midplane defect is resolved
Confirmation of the four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation and whether it applies to Kyber

arguments.statement: Lean Yes, with substantial risk: a SemiAnalysis-reported delay to 2028 (e64, e66, e98, e101) places Kyber's launch inside the 2028 window, so Kyber launching by 2028-12-31 remains plausible. Nvidia's roadmap-intact denials (e65, e72, e102) and the scrapped NVL72x2 alternative plus the reported cancellation of the four-die Rubin Ultra and the CPO-NVSwitch deferral to Feynman (new in this record, mapping to Kyber not stated) add downside risk that the 2028 slot slips further.
limitations: SemiAnalysis rumour, one source relayed by several outlets; not independent
Nvidia denies the delay without giving dates
2028 is a delay estimate, not a launch confirmation; slippage beyond 2028 is not excluded by the texts
Four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation and CPO-NVSwitch timing are not explicitly linked to Kyber
what_would_change_it: A Kyber NVL144 launch or shipment confirmation in 2028
A further delay beyond 2028, or confirmation of Feynman as the Kyber interconnect path
Nvidia or a filing giving a dated Kyber roadmap
Independent evidence that the PCB midplane manufacturability problem is solved

answer.reason: The record is the same SemiAnalysis report already held in e101, relayed by The Decoder, so the Kyber delay and NVL72x2 scrapping are the same claim and not independent. The new items (four-die Rubin Ultra cancelled, CPO-NVSwitch deferred to Feynman, more Oberon-Rubin racks) are rumour-level condition changes that move the risk on the Kyber launch questions v11 and v13, so both are updated with arguments. No separate investment judgement is needed; the record does not change the Kyber questions' underlying investment view beyond these conditions.
